request.system_message:
You abstract all predicate definitions in one semantic cluster into exactly one reusable, mechanism-level predicate conforming to predicate-definition/v2.

Read every member's complete definition, ordered parameters, assertion conditions, and exclusion conditions. Identify the shared underlying behavioral mechanism. Generalize concrete tasks, tools, files, services, and scenarios while retaining the logical constraints needed by that mechanism. Prefer a genuinely shared mechanism over similar vocabulary or a common topic. For example, specific action-result checks can generalize to verification of action effects; feedback-driven adjustments can generalize to revision of actions in response to feedback; concrete conflict-handling operations can generalize to conflict identification and resolution.

Cover the common semantics of the members with a concrete, observable, decidable mechanism. Preserve necessary behavioral direction and causal relationships; distinguish the roles of reasoning, action, and observation; retain important differences between attempting an effect and successfully achieving it; retain essential preconditions, assertion conditions, and exclusions with real distinguishing value. Avoid task-specific restrictions, vacuous generalizations, and mechanisms unsupported by the source members. This is Predicate Abstraction / Generalization: it may generalize multiple specific behaviors and does not require the bidirectional logical equivalence used by Registry Revision MERGE.

All members belong to the same arity group. The generated predicate MUST have exactly the cluster arity: len(parameters) == cluster.arity. Allowed parameter types are reasoning, action, observation, reasoning[], action[], observation[]. A homogeneous collection parameter counts as one argument. Preserve interpretable semantic roles and ordered argument relationships. You may rename parameters to express the common mechanism. Parameter names must be distinct lower_snake_case identifiers.

Always generate exactly one final predicate, including for singleton clusters and clusters with internal differences. For differing members, find the most reasonable common mechanism covering the group and preserve meaningful distinguishing conditions as far as possible. Never declare the members incompatible or impossible to merge. Never suggest splitting the cluster, deleting members, human handling, or multiple candidates. Never return incompatible, skip, failed, rejected, null, an empty predicate, or any status/reason wrapper. Do not add evaluation scores or explanations.

Return exactly one JSON object containing exactly these five fields:
{
  "name": "UPPER_SNAKE_CASE_NAME",
  "definition": "Complete, precise semantic definition.",
  "parameters": [
    {
      "name": "parameter_name",
      "type": "reasoning",
      "description": "Precise ordered argument role."
    }
  ],
  "assertion_conditions": ["Explicit observable condition."],
  "exclusion_conditions": ["Distinguishing exclusion condition."]
}
The example illustrates structure only; the actual ordered parameter count must equal the input cluster arity. The predicate name must be UPPER_SNAKE_CASE and must not conflict with any previously generated predicate name. Definition and parameter descriptions must be complete nonempty strings. Parameters must be a nonempty ordered typed array; each parameter must contain exactly name, type, description. Assertion conditions must contain at least one explicit nonempty condition. Exclusion conditions may be an empty array. Neither condition list may contain duplicates. Use English for all text. Output JSON only, with no Markdown or additional text.

Name: RECOVERS_UNUSABLE_CHECK_RESULT_VIA_METHOD_DIAGNOSIS_AND_ALTERNATIVE_RETRIEVAL. UPPER_SNAKE. Is long okay. Could be "RECOVERS_INCONCLUSIVE_CHECK_THROUGH_METHOD_DIAGNOSIS_AND_ALTERNATIVE_RETRIEVAL". Ensure not conflict. Fine.

Definition: "An executed information-retrieval check yields no usable information; reasoning attributes this to a concrete limitation of the check's method or tooling rather than to genuine absence/defect in inspected state; follow-up action retrieves same intended information using materially different technique." Include maybe check not necessarily "executed" but observation. Parameters: unusable_check_observation observation; method_limitation_diagnosis reasoning; alternative_retrieval_action action. Maybe 4 action follows diagnosis? Essential causal relation. Add "The alternative action is motivated by and addresses the diagnosed limitation." Could be condition. Need not overly specific. Exclusion:

Need JSON only.

parsed_response.name: RECOVERS_UNUSABLE_CHECK_RESULT_VIA_METHOD_DIAGNOSIS_AND_ALTERNATIVE_RETRIEVAL
parsed_response.definition: An executed information-retrieval check yields no usable information; the reasoning attributes this outcome to a concrete limitation of the check's method or tooling rather than to a genuine absence or defect in the inspected state; and a follow-up action retrieves the same intended information through a materially different technique or invocation.

parameters.name: unusable_check_observation
parameters.description: The observation reporting that the original check produced no interpretable information, including empty or missing output, an unparseable result, or an error indicating that a required command or tool is unavailable or unsupported.

parameters.name: method_limitation_diagnosis
parameters.description: The reasoning that identifies a concrete limitation of the check's method or tooling, such as unsupported syntax, wrong format, symlink handling, or an unavailable command, as the cause of the unusable result.

parameters.name: alternative_retrieval_action
parameters.description: The follow-up action that targets the same intended information as the original check and uses a materially different technique or invocation to retrieve it.

assertion_conditions: The observation reports that the original check produced no usable information, such as empty output, absent entries, an unparseable result, or an error stating that the command or tool relied on is unavailable or unsupported.
The reasoning identifies a concrete limitation of the original check's method or tooling as the cause of the unusable result rather than attributing it to the inspected state.
The alternative retrieval action addresses the diagnosed limitation and retrieves the same intended information using a materially different technique or invocation.
A causal sequence is present in which the unusable check result prompts the method diagnosis, and the diagnosis motivates the alternative retrieval action.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning attributes the unusable result to an actual defect or genuine absence in the inspected system rather than to a limitation of the check's method or tooling.
The follow-up action repeats the same method or uses only cosmetic variations of it.
No reasoning distinguishes a tooling artifact from a genuine finding about the inspected state.
The original observation already supplies the intended information, so no alternative retrieval is required.
The follow-up action targets information different from that sought by the original check or is otherwise unrelated to the diagnosed limitation.
